request.spec:
A button downloads the claims as a CSV file: a header line person,number,date,amount,due,status,period
then one line per claim, people in list order and each person's claims oldest first, retired people
included whether shown or not, with the figures as the screen shows them (an empty number, period or
n/a as it is). Quoting and line ends as the people export.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A button downloads the claims as a CSV file: a header line person,number,date,amount,due,status,period
then one line per claim, people in list order and each person's claims oldest first, retired people
included whether shown or not, with the figures as the screen shows them (an empty number, period or
n/a as it is). Quoting and line ends as the people export.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
There's now an "Export claims (CSV)" button (`data-testid="export-claims"`) next to "Export people", and all 4 acceptance tests pass in `bin/e2e`.

It's a front-end-only change in `src/main/frontend/src/app/features/people/people.ts`; the server and stored data didn't need to change. The file starts with the header `person,number,date,amount,due,status,period`, then has one line per claim:

- **Order:** people are in list order, including retired people even when "Show retired" is off. Each person's claims are oldest first, the reverse of the newest-first order on screen.
- **Values match what each claim's row shows:**
  - The due uses the same calculation the screen uses, and shows `n/a` when there's no rate.
  - A draft has an empty number.
  - The period is the one containing the claim's due-by date, or empty if no period does.
- **Format:** it uses the same CSV line builder (`csvLine`) as the people export, so quoting and `\n` line endings are identical. The file is named `claims-<sheet>.csv`.

I also moved the people export's download code into a shared `download()` helper that both buttons now use.
